description_ru: Две соседки спорят из-за старого дерева, но находят достойный компромисс, учитывающий память и безопасность.
text:
Mrs Alder: Good morning, Mr Patel. I wonder if you have a moment. It concerns the chestnut tree.
Rohan: Of course, Mrs Alder. Is something wrong?
Mrs Alder: Not wrong, exactly. But its branches now hang over my greenhouse, and the council's letter says you intend to have it felled.
Rohan: Ah. I did apply, yes. I'm sorry you heard it from a letter rather than from me.
Mrs Alder: I confess that did sting a little. That tree was here before either of us.
Rohan: It was, and I'm fond of it too. The trouble is the roots. The surveyor says they've begun lifting the foundations at the back of my house. There's a crack above the kitchen window you could slip a coin into.
Mrs Alder: Good heavens. I had no idea it was that serious.
Rohan: Neither did I until March. The repair estimate is nearly twelve thousand pounds, and the insurers won't pay while the tree remains.
Mrs Alder: I see. Has anyone suggested pruning the roots, rather than removing the whole thing?
Rohan: The surveyor mentioned it, but he thinks it would destabilise the tree and make it dangerous in a gale. Which would be worse for both of us.
Mrs Alder: Hm. My late husband planted a little oak behind it in 1987, and I'd hate for that to be damaged during any felling.
Rohan: I wasn't aware of that. I'll make certain the contractors work around it. In fact, if you like, I could pay for a replacement tree in the front garden, something with gentler roots.
Mrs Alder: That's a generous offer. What did you have in mind?
Rohan: A rowan, perhaps. Birds adore them, and the berries are lovely in autumn.
Mrs Alder: My husband would have approved. Though I'd like to choose the spot myself, if I may.
Rohan: Naturally. Shall we say we'll walk the garden together this Saturday and mark it out?
Mrs Alder: One more thing. If any branches fall during the work, my greenhouse will need a new pane or two.
Rohan: Send me the bill and consider it settled. I would also hate to lose your tomatoes.
Mrs Alder: You drive a gentle bargain for a man with a cracked kitchen.
Mrs Alder: I'd like that. And Mr Patel, next time, please knock on my door before the council writes to me.
Rohan: You have my word. I'll even bring the biscuits.
Mrs Alder: Ginger, if you've any sense.
Rohan: Ginger it is. And thank you for being so reasonable about this. I expected a much harder conversation.
Mrs Alder: So did I, to be honest. But it is difficult to stay cross with someone who admits he should have knocked first.

Дифтонг: начните с открытого «а» и скользните к «у», не заканчивайте на «в».
Дифтонг: от нейтрального «э» к «у», губы округляются к концу, не русское чистое «о».

questions.question: What does Rohan plan to do with the chestnut tree?
Why does he want to do it?
questions.answer: The roots are damaging the foundations of his house.

questions.question: What did Mrs Alder's husband plant?
What replacement does Rohan offer?
questions.answer: A rowan tree in the front garden.
